overall_summary: Space and extreme cosmic phenomena (specifically exoplanets with bizarre environmental conditions) are the clear channel drivers, frequently securing 700 to 1,000+ views. Conversely, psychology and cognitive brain facts (such as fake memories and songs stuck in your head) consistently underperform, rarely breaking 100 views even when re-uploaded with different durations.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,017 views), 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) represent the highest tier of views and engagement on the channel.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme space environments, focusing on mind-bending physical properties, extreme weather, and cosmic horror elements.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees' (302 views) and 'Why Your Head Is Older Than Your Feet' (264 views) perform significantly better than standard trivia.
winning_patterns.action: Frame historical or physical facts as direct contradictions to common sense in the first 2 seconds.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' was uploaded three times across different dates and lengths, peaking at only 53 views. 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs...' stalled at 71 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from cognitive biases and brain hacks unless they can be framed through a highly dramatic, cinematic storytelling lens.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (118-183 views) and 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' (69 views) fail to capture the viral velocity of cosmic topics.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid standard encyclopedia facts; instead, focus on cinematic animal survival narratives or extreme evolutionary defense mechanisms.

next_video.reason: Leverages the high-performing space category with a cinematic, high-stakes 'what-if' hook. The 21-second format matches the duration of our top-performing exoplanet videos.

experiment: Test a cinematic 'Survival Guide' format for extreme space environments (e.g., 'How to Survive 5 Seconds on the Planet of Burning Ice') to merge the high-performing exoplanet topic with active, high-retention storytelling.
